subject: net
title: IP fragmentation
procedure: Fragmenting IPv4 packets (offset, MF flag, length)
promptTemplate: Give a packet size, header length and one or more MTUs along the path. easy: one MTU. medium: two MTUs in a row. exam: header with options and fragmenting again. Asked for: number of fragments, total length, fragment offset (in 8-byte units), MF flag. When checking: is the payload per fragment divisible by 8? Are the offsets cumulative? Does the last fragment have MF=0?
answerFormat: Table: fragment | total length | offset | MF.

drills.prompt: An IPv4 packet has a total length of 4000 bytes and a 20-byte header (no options). It must cross a link with MTU 1500. Into how many fragments is it split?
drills.explanation: Payload 3980 bytes; at most 1480 bytes of payload per fragment (1500 − 20, divisible by 8): 1480 + 1480 + 1020.

drills.prompt: An IPv4 packet has a total length of 4000 bytes and a 20-byte header (no options). It must cross a link with MTU 1500. What is the fragment offset of the third fragment (in 8-byte units)?
An IPv4 packet has a total length of 4000 bytes and a 20-byte header (no options). It must cross a link with MTU 1500. What is the total length of the last fragment?
drills.explanation: Remaining payload 3980 − 2960 = 1020 bytes, plus the 20-byte header.

drills.prompt: Which fragments have the MF (more fragments) flag set to 0?
